title: What Does It Mean When A Dog Play-Bows?
description:
Front legs down, rear end up — this pose is basically a universal language.

script: Front legs flat on the ground, rear end up in the air, tail wagging, that goofy pose is actually one of the clearest signals in the entire dog communication system. It's called a play bow, and it means exactly one thing: everything that happens next is play, not a real fight. Dogs use this specific pose because it's unmistakable, it's physically very different from anything used in real aggression, so there's no room for confusion between species or even between a dog and a cat or a human. It's also a reset button mid-play, if things get a little too rough, a dog will drop back into a play bow to say, we're still just playing, don't worry. Researchers consider it one of the best examples of a genuinely universal animal signal, recognized and used the same way by dogs regardless of breed, age, or background. So that silly bow before the chaos starts? That's your dog being incredibly clear on purpose. Want more real dog behavior insight? The link's below.
